title: On the Chvátal–Gomory closure of a compact convex set
contribution: Proves that the Chvátal–Gomory closure of every non-empty compact convex set is a rational polytope, settling Schrijver's 1980 question for irrational polytopes and generalizing the authors' own ellipsoid and strictly-convex results (read: arXiv v1).
problem_entry: A classical open question quoted verbatim from Schrijver's discussion section, plus convex IPs whose second-order-cone sets have irrational generators; the named obstacle is irrationality (p. 2).
key_idea: Strengthen the inductive face property to CC(F_v,S) = H_v ∩ CC(K,S'), handle the irrational part through the integer affine hull aff_I and Kronecker density, then show only finitely many cuts can cut interior vertices of a boundary-exact approximation (pp. 3-4, 16-17).
assumptions: K non-empty compact convex in R^n, no rationality; compactness justified in footnote 2 because integer hulls of general convex sets need not be polyhedra (pp. 2-3).
proof_devices: Dirichlet simultaneous approximation to lift a face's CG cut to a CG cut of K (Lemma 3.3, Prop. 3.1, pp. 4-7)
unimodular normal form (0..0,1,alpha_1..alpha_r) with {1,alpha} Q-independent; D(v) = dimension of smallest rational subspace (Lemma 3.5, pp. 8-9)
Kronecker density to build D(v)+1 integer vectors near v whose CG cuts separate F_v minus aff_I(H_v) (Prop. 3.2, pp. 8-12)
measure-zero choice of a single equation representing integer points of an affine space (Lemma 4.1, pp. 12-14)
finite subcover of the sphere of directions (Prop. 4.1, pp. 14-15)
finitely many faces of a polytope meet relbd(K) (Lemma 4.2, pp. 15-16)
induction on dimension; undominated cuts must cut an interior vertex, bounding their norm by 1/delta (Thm. 5.1, pp. 15-17)
positioning: Generalizes Schrijver (rational polytopes), Dey-Vielma (ellipsoids) and Dadush-Dey-Vielma (strictly convex); credits Schrijver's boundary observation as crucial; proof 'similar in parts' to their previous one but with new diophantine components (pp. 1-3).
writing: Three-sentence abstract; theorem plus numbered proof roadmap keyed to sections before any proof; prose intuition before the hardest proposition; no conclusion section (pp. 1, 3-4, 9, 17).
limits_future: Compactness required (footnote 2, p. 2); existential proof with no bound on the number of cuts or algorithm (not discussed); no future directions stated in this version.

title: On the practical strength of two-row tableau cuts
contribution: A controlled computational study showing that lifted type 2 triangle cuts from two tableau rows nearly reach the two-row hull on synthetic dense instances but add almost nothing over GMI and two-row split cuts on MIPLIB, and that tableau density and important continuous non-basics explain the difference.
problem_entry: Theory (Basu et al.) predicts type 2 triangle closures far stronger than split closures; the original goal of a useful small two-row cut subset was 'too ambitious' and was restricted to asking which MIP characteristics make triangles useful (pp. 2, 5).
key_idea: Heuristic type 2 triangle generator with monoidal strengthening, evaluated in a stripped protocol (one round, first tableau, all cuts, no selection) with %gap and leave-one-family-out importance Imp(X) along an instance ladder from 'perfect' two-row instances to modified MIPLIB (pp. 6-11).
assumptions: Two-row relaxations (1) and (2) with fractional f; theory assumes continuous non-basics, no bounds; numerical safeguards 0.001 on fractionality and distance of f to the boundary; C++ with CPLEX 10.0 (pp. 1-2, 10, 12-13).
proof_devices: cited theory only: classification of maximal lattice-free sets in R^2 (Prop. 2.1, p. 4), intersection cuts (p. 4), monoidal strengthening with closed form of Basu et al. (p. 5), closure comparison (Thm. 2.1, p. 5)

own construction: two tiny 2-D integer programs plus iterative validity test to find a facet of conv(Y^2), then Euclidean-algorithm lifting of a third ray (pp. 6-9); facet-defining only with three rays (p. 9)
experiments: 90 'perfect' two-row instances (T 97.99% vs G 75.10%); 28 MIPLIB 3.0 instances (G 31.62, S 33.15, T 20.53, GST 40.49); Atamturk-generator families A-D isolating integer non-basics with identical cuts; bounds; density and rows with entanglement p01/p11; MIPLIB.D and MIPLIB.D.C modified benchmarks; RSD and generated-vs-binding counts reported; no running times (pp. 10-24, 28-30).
positioning: Distinguished from Espinoza and from Basu-Bonami-Cornuejols-Margot in three points each, chiefly that explaining which MIP characteristics matter is the primary goal; tests theory partly by the authors themselves; cut selection set aside as its own topic (pp. 2-3, 10).
writing: Restricted question displayed with '(simpler?)'; 'possible interpretations' bullets after each table; contradiction between tables turned into four numbered questions; negative verdict stated plainly in abstract and conclusion (pp. 1-2, 12-13, 16, 25).
limits_future: Only type 2 triangles, one per ray pair, one round, 'clearly not exhaustive'; future: facets of (1) not obtained by lifting, cut selection (few cuts bind), m-row relaxations for dense instances (pp. 10, 25).

title: How good are sparse cutting-planes?
contribution: Measures the loss from using only k-sparse cuts by the distance d(P,P^k) and proves vertex-count upper bounds with three phases, near-matching lower bounds for random 0/1 polytopes, large distance for random packing IPs, and that sparse cuts are at least as good (sometimes much better) in extended formulations (read: arXiv v1).
problem_entry: Commercial solvers favour sparse cuts (personal communications), but 'very few studies' exist; the two-sided trade-off (LP speed vs gap closure) is reduced to the one-sided geometric question of how well k-sparse cuts approximate the integer hull (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Define P^k as the intersection of P + R^{I-bar} over k-subsets and fix a well-defined measure d(P,P^k) after discarding objective and volume ratios; bound it by the number of vertices, show tightness by random polytopes and a negative packing class (pp. 2-6).
assumptions: P in [0,1]^n wlog, given by t vertices, l2 norm; random uniform 0/1 points with t in a stated range and 64 <= k <= n; (n,m,M)-PIP packing distribution; constants not optimized (pp. 2, 4-6).
proof_devices: closest-point separating hyperplane (Obs. 3.1, p. 6)
unbiased randomized sparsification of the dense normal with Bernstein, union bound over vertices and Markov (Lemma 3.2, Claims 3.4-3.6, pp. 6-8)
averaging k-sparse weakenings of a halfspace over all supports (Lemma 3.8, pp. 8-9)
alpha-tough polytopes plus new anticoncentration lemma via bucketing coefficients, finite integer direction set from Ziegler for union bound (Lemmas 4.2-4.6, pp. 9-11; App. C, pp. 18-19)
order statistics plus Chebyshev, continuous-to-discrete coupling, and averaging randomly thinned 0/1 points to pass from approximate to actual containment (Lemmas 5.3-5.5, pp. 12-15)
binary-tree extended formulation with 3-sparse constraints (Prop. 2.5, p. 16)
pointer to generic chaining for structured bounds (Obs. 3.7, p. 8)
experiments: One small computation: n = 10, 150 random binary points on sum x = 5; PORTA describes each P + R^{I-bar}; vertices of P^k not computable, so a lower bound on d(P,P^k) is found by 'shooting' along 20,000 random directions plus ±e/sqrt(n) (p. 3; App. B, p. 17).
positioning: Only Andersen-Weismantel zero-coefficient cuts as explicit prior work; packing instances from Kaparis-Letchford; probability tools from textbooks; practitioner evidence via personal communications; no critique of predecessors (pp. 1, 5, 16-17).
writing: Examples first, then a 'Main Results' section with all theorems and plain-language readings before the proofs; explicit hedges on worst case and unoptimized constants; 'Surprisingly' frames the gap and the closed form (pp. 1, 3-6).
limits_future: Worst-case in the number of vertices, says little about structured polytopes; constants not optimized; no conclusion section; implicit directions: generic chaining for structured P, denser cuts for packing, extended formulations (pp. 4-6, 8).

title: Design and verify: a new scheme for generating cutting-planes
contribution: Introduces verification closures (design an integral cut, verify it by emptiness of M(P ∩ {cx >= d+1})) and maps their strength: almost admissible, stronger than M, GC and N0 for any admissible M, comparisons among GC/SC/N0/N/N+ versions, rank bounds on A_n, rank 1 for clique-type stable-set inequalities, Theta(n) for TSP, and integral hull in R^2 for the verification GC closure.
problem_entry: Generic cuts are produced 'almost blindly' by black boxes; using the same black box to verify a designed cut can be strictly stronger because M(P ∩ {cx >= d+1}) can be smaller than M(P) ∩ {cx >= d+1} (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Define the V-closure as the intersection of all verifiable integral inequalities and analyse it axiomatically over Pokutta-Schulz admissible operators, pairing strength results with rank lower bounds (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: Admissible cutting-plane procedures (Pokutta-Schulz axioms) plus an added Strong Homogeneity for general IPs, justified in Remark 1; rational polytopes; each result tagged with the properties it uses; short verification for the V-closure not proved (pp. 3-5).
proof_devices: perturbation c + tau a to transfer emptiness on a face to a verifiable cut of P (Lemma 2, Thm. 1, p. 5)
comparison of compact convex sets through support functions on integer directions (Lemma 3, p. 6)
canonical infeasible polytope A_n and half-integral families A_n^k for strictness and rank lower bound by induction (Prop. 4, Lemma 14, Thm. 4, pp. 7, 11-12)
gadget Q = conv(P x {1} ∪ [0,1]^n x {0}) with V-closure integral iff L(P) empty (Lemma 10, Prop. 9, p. 9)
face-fixing lemma: validity on every x_i = 1 face implies validity for the V-closure (Lemma 16, p. 12)
embedding A_{n/8} into the TSP polytope by coordinate flips and duplications (p. 15)
planar lattice geometry: lattice-free parallelograms, splits, minimally infeasible points (Thm. 8, pp. 15-17)
positioning: Builds on Pokutta-Schulz admissible operators and classical rank results (Chvatal-Cook-Hartmann, Cook-Dash, Lovasz-Schrijver); only related idea Cook-Coullard-Turan, whose potential 'has not been further investigated'; uses Dadush-Dey-Vielma for GC of convex sets (pp. 2-4, 11-15).
writing: Practice motivation, one-paragraph definition and a 3-dimensional example of the payoff before theory; section-by-section contribution paragraph; one figure summarizing all relations; conclusion balances 'very strong' and 'not unrealistically strong' (pp. 1-3, 7, 17).
limits_future: Short verification not established; no design procedure and no computation; TSP rank stays Theta(n); future: verification for mixed-integer problems via projected GC cuts (pp. 5, 14-15, 17).

method_links.note: strength results paired with rank lower bounds showing the scheme is not unrealistically strong (A_n, TSP)
